newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Low prices hit China metals corp's 1996 net.
newsitem.headline: Low prices hit China metals corp's 1996 net.

text.p: Low prices nearly obliterated profits at China National Non-Ferrous Metals Industry Corp (CNNC), vice-president Chen Shengnian said on Monday.

Profit at CNNC, the government body responsible for the country's non-ferrous metal production, amounted to five million yuan ($602,409) in 1996 compared to about two billion yuan ($240.96 million) in 1995, Chen told reporters after speaking at a China non-ferrous metals fair here.
A steep dip last year in non-ferrous metals prices, particularly copper, had seriously affected CNNC's profits, he said.
"Last year we had big problems as we imported a lot of (expensive raw material) and the finished product prices were low," Chen added.
"CNNC is only seeking reasonable prices for all non-ferrous metals, not too high and not too low, stability is important for reasonable profits," he said.
This year, prices for finished products have remained weak but production costs in China have also come down, making the outlook brighter, Chen said.
"At present, the prices are reasonable," Chen said.
